answer: Reputation-weighted escrow release. Each new identity must finance its first 30 transactions from a shared pool that pays out only after counterparties confirm delivery, so a clone farm’s payout lag hits its cash nadir before any revenue arrives. Because payouts route through rotating settlement nodes, an attacker must keep every clone liquid through that lag, and the oasis of confirmed history only opens after real counterparties validate. Per-identity enforcement costs the attacker the float plus a zephyr of delayed capital, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
